<reason>PRO won the meaning of personal medical choices. CON redefined dignity as equal standing and proved valid consent can coexist with a wrongful paid-sterilization scheme, forcing a concession. But CON then conceded dignity never overrules competent refusal, pregnancy, or relief from agony, leaving only regulation of a discriminatory offer where sterilization on equal terms remains. PRO's deals vs bodies distinction kept the core bodily decision with autonomy, which is what the motion is about.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 offer/body distinction answered A's forced concession: admitting valid consent yet banning the bigoted offer, then showing her sterilization choice stands so dignity governs offers while autonomy governs bodies.</best_rebuttal>
